entries.knowledge: The general non-desklamp procedure has now carried the same temperature-transformation guidance through three successive edits, and the current edit re-inserts it into the acquire step: after acquiring the exact target, go to the fridge for cooling or the microwave for heating; if the explicit cool-object-with-fridge / heat-object-with-microwave action is already admissible, perform it immediately while holding the target and without first inserting it; open the appliance only when needed; do not treat moving the object in, closing or reopening the door, examining the appliance, or toggling it as completing the temperature change; and after the action succeeds once, go directly to the destination. The observed response when the exact target was located and the explicit action was admissible while holding is consistent: the Candidate conditioned the held object directly and skipped the appliance-insertion and door-toggling the Parent performed. In a cool-tomato-to-microwave task the Candidate cooled the held tomato at the fridge and finished in 10 steps versus the Parent's 18, whose excess came mostly from search cycling. In a heat-tomato-to-fridge pair with identical fridge contents (both took the same tomato at the same step), the Parent inserted the tomato, then repeatedly closed and reopened the microwave and only heated it at step 36, placing at step 39, whereas the Candidate heated the held tomato with a single action at the still-closed microwave and placed it in 8 steps. In a second heat-tomato pair the Candidate heated the held tomato at the closed microwave and finished in 7 steps while the Parent first opened the microwave and finished in 8. In a cool-plate pair both held the plate, but the Candidate performed the cool action with the fridge unopened whereas the Parent opened it first; the Candidate spent one extra step elsewhere (9 vs 8), so the unopened-door behaviour did not by itself reduce steps there. This reproduces earlier observations from the two prior temperature edits, where the Candidate heated or cooled the held object at the closed appliance and largely avoided the Parent's insert-and-toggle cycles with large step savings (hot-potato 7 vs 14, heat-tomato 7 vs 21, heat-egg, cool-pot, hot-apple). The conditionality remains: in the current heat-apple task the apple was absent from the fridge, countertops and cabinets, neither execution ever reached a temperature action, and both hit the 50-step limit; earlier heat-plate and hot-mug cases likewise failed on search rather than on conditioning, and the Candidate avoided heating a cup when the requested mug was absent. When the appliance was already open as a result of search, the Candidate still conditioned the held object, so the condition-while-holding behaviour does not depend on the door being closed. Locating the exact target remains a precondition for any temperature-guidance benefit, every task was run once, and the current diff also tightened the search step in the same edit.

The general non-desklamp search step has been rewritten repeatedly. An earlier edit replaced broad open-closed-containers text with a single-pass family sweep: open each closed container once, spread across distinct receptacle families, switch to a different uninspected family before revisiting any earlier location, and keep the sweep within the step budget. The current edit tightens the same step further: treat each individual closed container (cabinet, drawer, fridge, microwave, safe, etc.) and each open surface as a separate candidate; do not treat a container family as finished merely because one or two of its members were empty; after arriving at a receptacle that is already open and empty, or whose visible contents match an already-inspected location, do not open, re-examine or linger there and leave immediately for an uninspected receptacle; and if the same small set of locations keeps reappearing in recent observations without yielding the target, stop revisiting them and continue to new candidates while the budget allows. The observed response in the current pairs was mixed. In a two-book-to-desk task with identical setup, in which both books lay on the bed, the Parent cycled among the desk, shelves and drawers and hit the 50-step limit without ever going to the bed, whereas the Candidate eventually left the recurring set, reached the bed at step 33, and delivered both books sequentially, succeeding in 40 steps. In a two-creditcard-to-safe task the Candidate went straight to the desk that held both creditcards and finished in 9 steps, versus the Parent's 24 steps that first opened drawers 1-8. When the requested object was absent or unlocated, however, the revised language was not followed and gave no benefit: in a heat-apple task the Candidate cycled among the fridge, countertop 1/2 and cabinet 1/2 just as the Parent did and hit the 50-step limit without switching to uninspected drawers or shelves and without stopping the revisits, and in a cool-tomato task the Candidate merely searched somewhat more directly (fridge then countertop 1 then countertop 2, 10 steps) while the Parent looped (18 steps), though both found the tomato at the same location. Earlier evidence for the same sweep lineage stands: it produced two rescues where the exact target lay in a family the Parent never reached (a butterknife on countertop 2 and a soapbar on shelf 1), but it did not reliably prevent cycling and step-limit failure when the target was absent and sometimes added steps by revisiting already-seen empty locations. Notably the current skill carried no explicit multi-instance find-and-place step, yet both two-instance tasks succeeded, so the search guidance plus the Actor's behaviour can support sequential delivery when the source is found. The current diff also added temperature guidance in the same edit, so the multi-instance and search differences cannot be attributed to the search clause alone; each task was run once.
